Company.title: Company
Company.description: Represents a company using the AttendWise application.

subscriptionPlan.description: The subscription plan the company is on (e.g., Basic, Premium).

userLimit.description: Maximum number of users allowed for the company.

recordLimit.description: Maximum number of attendance records allowed for the company.

usedSlots.description: Number of user slots currently used by the company.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user within the AttendWise application.

companyId.description: Reference to the Company the user belongs to. (Relationship: Company 1:N User)

role.description: Role of the user within the company (e.g., Global Admin, Manager, Employee).

status.description: Status of the user account (e.g., pending, active).

AttendanceRecord.title: AttendanceRecord
AttendanceRecord.description: Represents an attendance record for a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the attendance record.

userId.description: Reference to the User this record belongs to. (Relationship: User 1:N AttendanceRecord)

type.description: Type of attendance event (e.g., Check-in, Check-out).

definition.description: Stores company information. The company 'id' is used as the document ID.

params.name: companyId
params.description: The unique identifier for the company.

definition.description: Stores user information. The user 'id' is used as the document ID. Includes denormalized 'companyId' for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user.

definition.description: Stores attendance records for a specific user.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user.

params.name: attendanceRecordId
params.description: The unique identifier for the attendance record.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to ensure authorization independence, clarity, and scalability, aligning with the specified principles. The structure prioritizes path-based ownership for private user data and employs membership maps for collaborative data access. Denormalization is used extensively to avoid `get()` calls in security rules, which enables atomic operations and simplifies debugging. Segregation is used to ensure all docs in a collection have the same security posture. Global roles are managed by a 'role' field within the user's document.
